newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: France's Chirac opposes national euro symbols.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac opposes national euro symbols.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday that France risked being flooded with banknotes bearing alien symbols if national emblems were allowed to appear on the future European single currency.
Chirac told reporters that EU leaders debated at their Dublin summit whether to put national logos on the euro banknotes, which were unveiled during the meeting.

He said British Prime Minister John Major, who has negotiated an opt-out from the single currency, had asked that up to a quarter of the banknote be reserved for national signs such as a portrait of Britain's queen.
"I'm not in favour of that idea for a simple reason: France is a country that receives lots of European tourists from the northern countries and Germany," Chirac said.

"Pretty soon, especially south of the Loire (river), there would only be banknotes with foreign Swedish or German effigies on them in circulation and there'd be no more French notes, which would be circulating elsewhere," he said.
He said that other countries with major tourism industries, such as Portugal, Spain and Italy, might suffer the same fate.
"So it seems to me more sensible to have a unitary banknote for everyone."

Chirac said he found the euro designs, which deliberately avoided any national landmarks, symbols or historic faces, "quite pretty", but he supported a call by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to make the notes more colourful.
"Chancellor Kohl made a very commonsense remark, like everything he says, that the colours are not bright enough, and that old people with poor eyesight could mix them up," the French leader said.
